data_fields.name: theme_name_pattern
data_fields.donor_constant: zone_DAY|NGT_STD|FGT|THR (theme table per zone, not read)

data_fields.name: zone_recheck_interval
data_fields.donor_constant: 5*1000 ms of game ticks (5 s at 1x)

data_fields.name: emitter_repeat_delay
data_fields.donor_constant: random_delay seconds x 1000, plus rand % random_delay_var

data_fields.name: emitter_day_window
data_fields.donor_constant: clock window from the vob (start to end)

data_fields.name: embellishment_on_mode_change
data_fields.donor_constant: into std from fight = BREAK; into fgt from thr = FILL; else NONE

data_fields.name: fallback_order
data_fields.donor_constant: zone then default zone; night then day; mode then weaker mode then std

best_idea: pick music from (zone, day or night, fight mode) through a fallback chain of named themes, and play a short fill or break when the fight mode changes, so the change is musical and not a hard cut
decision_why: Take the mode-and-fallback selection and the embellishment table, drive the change from the engage event instead of a 5-second poll, and use the server's zone name instead of the last-match scan.
acceptance: when a creature engages the player, the combat theme starts within one render chunk of the engage event (a client test asserts the mode change is handled in the event handler, not in a timer), with a fill played first; when the player leaves the fight, a break plays and the standard theme resumes.
